description: Tight live-bug rule for a VN learner sentence that combines an explicit yesterday marker, bare invite, and a specific dinner/cigars/fun run-on. It corrects invite -> invited, splits the sentence into three short sentences, and changes the coordinated activity to smoked cigars.
fp_risk_note: Low-medium risk. This is not a general run-on rewriter. It fires only on a full-sentence anchored frame: I invite my (best/close/old) friend to come to my house yesterday and we had dinner and optional transcript noise ('yet why and') we smoke cigars he had a lot of fun. The explicit yesterday marker licenses invite -> invited, the already-past 'had dinner' anchors the sequence, and the closed 'we smoke cigars he had a lot of fun' tail is split into two simple clauses. Present habitual, future invite plans, already-correct past forms, and other run-ons all abstain.

positive.input: I invite my best friend to come to my house yesterday and we had dinner and yet why and we smoke cigars he had a lot of fun
positive.expectedCorrection: I invited my best friend to come to my house yesterday. We had dinner and smoked cigars. He had a lot of fun.
positive.notes: Exact live input: fixes invite -> invited and does not leave the full run-on unchanged.

positive.input: I invite my friend to come to my house yesterday and we had dinner and we smoke cigars he had a lot of fun
positive.expectedCorrection: I invited my friend to come to my house yesterday. We had dinner and smoked cigars. He had a lot of fun.
positive.notes: Same anchored frame without the noisy 'yet why' transcript fragment.

positive.input: I invite my old friend to come to my house yesterday and we had dinner and yet why and we smoke cigars he had a lot of fun
positive.expectedCorrection: I invited my old friend to come to my house yesterday. We had dinner and smoked cigars. He had a lot of fun.
positive.notes: Same anchored frame with a closed friend modifier; preserves the modifier.
